batchName: Empire: The Five Good Emperors (AD 96-192) - Latin words
description: Written by hand from the chapter text: the Latin words it explains

questions.question: The Senate gave Trajan the title optimus princeps. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: He was the only emperor officially given it; it appears on coins from 105.

questions.question: What was the limes that Hadrian strengthened?
options: The frontier, with forts and watchtowers
questions.explanation: Hadrian’s Wall in Britain was part of it.
questions.sourceQuote: he strengthened the frontier (*limes*) with forts, watchtowers and constant drill for the troops.

questions.question: What were the alimenta that Trajan formalised?
options: Welfare for orphans and poor children
questions.explanation: They gave cash, food and schooling across Italy.
questions.sourceQuote: He formalised the *alimenta*, a welfare scheme giving cash, food and schooling to orphans and poor children across Italy.

questions.question: Antoninus Pius gave a last password: aequanimitas. What does it mean?
questions.explanation: He gave it to the officer of the night watch as he lay dying in 161.

questions.question: What was horror imperii, which Marcus Aurelius may have felt?
questions.explanation: He took power in 161 with reluctance and shared it with Lucius Verus.
questions.sourceQuote: a genuine 'fear of imperial power' (*horror imperii*)

questions.question: Under an earlier deal, the king of Dacia was a rex amicus. What was that?
options: A client king, a “friendly king” of Rome
questions.explanation: He received Roman money and experts, which senators saw as shameful tribute.
questions.sourceQuote: its king was recognised as a client king (*rex amicus*)

questions.question: What was the Forum Traiani?
options: The Forum of Trajan, Rome’s largest forum
questions.explanation: Built with loot from his wars, it was dedicated on 1 January 112.

questions.question: The Senate hesitated to make Hadrian a divus. What was a divus?
options: A god, a dead emperor honoured in worship
questions.explanation: Antoninus insisted, and was named Pius, “the dutiful”.
questions.sourceQuote: hesitated to declare Hadrian a god (*divus*)
